title: 2017 United States Marine Corps KC-130 crash
summary: The aircraft crashed during cruise at 20,000 feet over Mississippi. Investigation determined that improper repairs to a corroded inner-left propeller blade conducted in 2011 caused blade failure in flight. The failed blade penetrated the left fuselage, and through a cascade of damage events, caused the right horizontal stabilizer to be struck and removed. The forward fuselage subsequently separated from aerodynamic forces and the aircraft rapidly descended.
probable_cause: Improper repairs conducted in 2011 on a corroded propeller blade resulted in blade failure during cruise, leading to catastrophic structural damage and loss of control.

The forward fuselage separated and the aircraft rapidly descended in a flat spin.
